newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian students committed suicide at torture jail.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian students committed suicide at torture jail.

text.p: Six Ethiopian university students taken to a jail where torture was rampant killed themselves before they could be interrogated by Marxist military authorities, a court heard on Tuesday.

A prosecution witness, who cannot be identified under Ethiopian court rules, said the six students were taken to prison in 1977 by a former senior army officer now on trial for genocide and crimes against humanity.
Captain Legesse Asfaw was a member of the Dergue, Ethiopia's army junta which ruled the Horn of Africa nation from 1974, after ousting Emperor Haile Selassie, until 1991.
"Six university students, one of them a girl were brought to Dergue prison by Captain Legesse Asfaw and were handed over to a sergeant guarding the prison cell in 1977," the witness said.
"Two of them, a girl and a boy, slashed their throats with a broken part of a bottle and died instantly in front of the cell,"the witness told the court in Addis Ababa.
"The other four jumped into an open toilet pit in the small prison compound at the headquarters of the Dergue and died," he added.

The witness was testifying at the trial of 71 members of the Dergue. A total of 46 of the former officials of the Dergue are in the dock in Addis Ababa. Twenty-five others, including former Marxist ruler Mengistu Haile Mariam, are on trial in absentia.
The 71 face the death sentence if found guilty.
The witness, who faced tough cross examination by the defence lawyer of Legesse, insisted he had witnessed the incident while he was a prisoner of the Dergue at the time.
Legesse was one of Ethiopia's most powerful men during the Dergue era and was considered the right hand man of Mengistu, who now lives in exile in Zimbabwe.

The witness said he and other prisoners saw what had happened through a key-hole and since he was a medical orderly, he pleaded with the prison guard to let him help the the two students, who were bleeding profusely.
"I was let out of the cell, but as I tried to help them it was too late, both had severed the main artery along their neck and were dying," he said.
The witness said that the remaining four students jumped one after the other into a nearby open toilet pit used by prisoners and also died.
The witness said during his stay in prison, he was allowed to treat torture victims which gave him the opportunity to witness "the severity and the sadistic nature of the Dergue torture."
"I saw women prisoners with sticks shoved inside their private parts. I saw women who could no longer control their urine due to the severity of beatings and torture," he said.
The witness said he also saw prisoners whose bodies were burnt after kerosine was poured on them and then they were set alight.
"If a prisoner suffered the misfortune of a broken leg, arm or lost eye sight, he was executed without mercy," he said. "The reason was not to leave evidence behind."

The government says it holds 1,700 prisoners for alleged crimes under the Dergue.The only ones charged are those now on trial. The rest of the prisoners have been held for up to five years without charge.
The trial was adjourned to Thursday.
